context: Fixture-scope design for a suite whose cost is a per-test container and whose risk is what happens when that container is shared. Four distinct pieces of setup sit at one scope: a cheap logger, a mutation of a process-wide config singleton, a container plus migrations, and per-test seed data. Predicted baseline failure: the agent recommends moving the container to suite scope - correct, and the obvious half of the answer - without specifying the per-test data-reset mechanism that makes it safe, which is precisely why the team's earlier attempt was reverted. The globalConfig mutation is usually missed entirely: it is a shared surface that becomes dangerous only once setup stops running for every test.

checklist.name: Container moved to a wider scope
checklist.description: The container and its migrations are recommended at suite, file, or per-worker scope rather than per test, with the reasoning tied to the 25-second startup against 94 tests.

checklist.name: A concrete per-test reset mechanism is specified
checklist.description: The document names how each test gets a clean database on a shared container - transaction rollback per test, truncation between tests, a schema or database per worker, or uniquely namespaced rows. Recommending the wider scope without naming a mechanism scores zero on this criterion: that is the recommendation the team already tried and reverted, and the task asks specifically for this part.

checklist.name: Global config mutation identified as a shared surface
checklist.description: The document flags that AppTest mutates globalConfig, a process-wide object, and that this is currently masked by setup running before every test - so widening any scope leaves the flag set for tests that never asked for it. Omitting this scores zero; naming it only as a style issue rather than a scope hazard scores at most half.

checklist.name: Seed data kept per test or made independent
checklist.description: The catalogue and customer seeds are addressed: either kept per test, or moved wider with unique identifiers so two tests cannot collide on the same customer email. Recommending they move to suite scope unchanged - with a shared customer row every test writes against - scores zero.

checklist.name: Inheritance chain addressed with a concrete alternative
checklist.description: The four-level chain is called out and replaced with something specific - composable helpers or per-resource fixtures assembled where needed - rather than a general recommendation to reduce coupling. No alternative offered scores at most half.

checklist.name: Cheap correctly-scoped setup left alone
checklist.description: MUST NOT recommend churn without benefit. The logger created in BaseTest is inexpensive and stateless per test; the document either leaves it as is or explicitly says it needs no change. Recommending work on it alongside the real findings scores zero on this criterion.
